THE SAME SYSTEM AT FOUR SCALES
==================================================================================

SCALE 4: CANOPY (dendrology/)        30 m vertical    DECADES to CENTURIES
  Sunlight hits leaves. Carbon fixed. Wood accretes.
  Canopy gaps create successional mosaics.
  Keystone: mast-producing oaks → mammal/bird populations

          |  Leaf litter falls
          |  Dissolved organics leach
          v

SCALE 3: STREAM NETWORK (freshwater-biology/)    WATERSHED    YEARS to DECADES
  Water carries nutrients downhill. Allochthonous carbon
  (leaf litter) fuels headwater food webs.
  Keystone: predatory fish → invertebrate → algae cascades

          |  Sediment, nutrients settle
          |  Riparian roots stabilize banks
          v

SCALE 2: SOIL HORIZON (soil-science/)       0-2 m depth    CENTURIES to MILLENNIA
  Decomposition converts biomass to humus. Fungi and bacteria
  mineralize N, P, K. Mycorrhizae close the loop back to roots.
  Keystone: mycorrhizal fungi → nutrient access → plant survival

          |  Weathering products dissolve
          |  Groundwater carries Ca²⁺, HCO₃⁻ to coast
          v

SCALE 1: REEF ARCHITECTURE (coral-reefs/)     0-50 m depth    MILLENNIA to EPOCHS
  Dissolved Ca²⁺ + HCO₃⁻ arrive from continental weathering.
  Corals precipitate CaCO₃. Symbiotic algae drive the energy budget.
  Keystone: herbivorous fish → algae → coral light access

==================================================================================
  Energy source:     Solar radiation at every scale
  Currency:          Carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, water
  Organizing force:  Trophic structure + nutrient cycling + disturbance regime

MATERIAL FLOWS LINKING ALL FOUR SCALES
==========================================

    ATMOSPHERE
    (CO₂, N₂, O₂, H₂O vapor)
         |                ^
         | photosynthesis | respiration, transpiration
         v                |
  +========================+
  | FOREST CANOPY          |
  | dendrology/            |
  +========================+
    Fixes 5-15 t C/ha/yr.
    Intercepts 20-40% of rainfall.

         |                ^
         | litterfall     | nutrient uptake via
         | 3-8 t/ha/yr    | mycorrhizal network
         v                |

  +========================+
  | SOIL                   |
  | soil-science/          |
  +========================+
    Stores 100-300 t C/ha (top 1m).
    Mineralizes N: 50-150 kg/ha/yr.

         |                ^
         | leachate,      | riparian roots stabilize
         | groundwater    | banks, shade stream
         v                |

  +========================+
  | STREAM / RIVER         |
  | freshwater-biology/    |
  +========================+
    Transports 2-20 t sediment/km²/yr.
    Carries dissolved nutrients to coast.

         |
         | river discharge: dissolved Ca²⁺, HCO₃⁻, PO₄³⁻, SiO₂
         v

  +========================+
  | CORAL REEF             |
  | coral-reefs/           |
  +========================+
    Accretes 1-10 kg CaCO₃/m²/yr.
    Builds 3D structure over millennia.

The forest feeds the soil.
The soil feeds the stream.
The stream feeds the reef.
Deforest a hillside and the reef downstream gets smothered in sediment.

blocks.heading_context: ## Trophic Cascades — The Same Story Four Times
blocks.text:
THE CASCADE MECHANISM
======================

  Remove top predator
       |
       v
  Herbivore/consumer population EXPLODES (release from predation)
       |
       v
  Primary producer / basal resource COLLAPSES (overgrazing/overconsumption)
       |
       v
  Habitat structure degrades → cascading loss of associated species

blocks.heading_context: ## Bridge to Computing — Ecosystems as Distributed Systems
blocks.text:
ECOSYSTEM CONCEPT              DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS ANALOG
===========================================================================

Keystone species               Single point of failure (SPOF)
  Remove wolves → cascade        Remove a core service → cascade
  Remove mycorrhizae → forest    Remove auth service → nothing works
  dies slowly

Trophic cascade                Cascading failure
  Bass removed → minnows         Load balancer fails → backend
  explode → algae crashes →      overloads → database saturates →
  lake goes anoxic                timeout cascade → full outage

Biodiversity / redundancy      Service redundancy / replicas
  Multiple predator species      Multiple replicas behind LB
  = functional redundancy        = no single point of failure
  Lose one, another fills role   Lose one, traffic shifts

Succession                     System bootstrapping
  Pioneer species prepare        Init containers prepare env
  environment for next stage     for application containers
  Each stage depends on prior    Each boot stage depends on prior

Nutrient cycling               Resource pooling / GC
  N, P, C recycled through      Memory, connections recycled
  decomposition → uptake loop    through pool → use → return loop
  Leak = eutrophication          Leak = resource exhaustion

Disturbance regime             Chaos engineering
  Fire maintains mosaic;         Chaos Monkey kills instances;
  suppressing fire → fuel        suppressing failures → fragility
  accumulation → catastrophe     accumulation → cascading outage

Carrying capacity              Rate limiting / back-pressure
  Population exceeds resource    Requests exceed capacity →
  → crash (overshoot)            → queue overflow → crash

Resilience                     Fault tolerance
  Speed of return to steady      Recovery time objective (RTO)
  state after perturbation       after incident

Phase shift (reef → algae)     Split-brain / data corruption
  System locks into degraded     System locks into inconsistent
  state; cannot self-recover     state; cannot self-heal
  Requires external forcing      Requires manual intervention
  to restore original state      to restore consistency
===========================================================================
